mainEntity.name: Why does dividing complex numbers use the conjugate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiplying the denominator by its conjugate z̄ turns it into the real number |z|², eliminating i from the denominator — the complex equivalent of rationalizing a square root.

mainEntity.name: What is the geometric meaning of multiplying complex numbers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiplication multiplies the moduli and adds the arguments — geometrically, it scales and rotates. This is exactly what De Moivre's theorem generalizes to powers and roots.

mainEntity.name: Why does a complex number have n different nth roots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because angles that differ by a full turn (2π) describe the same point, but raising to the nth power multiplies the angle by n — so n different starting angles, spaced 2π/n apart, all land on the same result.

mainEntity.name: What is the complex conjugate used for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Besides division, z·z̄ = |z|² always gives a real number, which is essential for finding magnitudes, normalizing vectors, and in signal processing for computing power from a complex amplitude.

mainEntity.name: How is Euler's formula related to polar form?

acceptedAnswer.text: Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ lets polar form r(cos θ + i sin θ) be written compactly as r·e^(iθ) — the same number, and the form that makes multiplication, powers and roots most natural.

mainEntity.name: How do you divide complex numbers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, which makes the denominator a real number. (3 + 4i) ÷ (1 − 2i) = (−5 + 10i) ÷ 5 = −1 + 2i.

mainEntity.name: What is the magnitude or absolute value of a complex number?

acceptedAnswer.text: The modulus |a + bi| = √(a² + b²). For 3 + 4i it is √25 = 5. Magnitude, modulus and absolute value are the same thing.

mainEntity.name: How do you convert a complex number to polar form?

acceptedAnswer.text: Find r = √(a² + b²) and θ = atan2(b, a), then write r(cos θ + i sin θ) or r∠θ. For 3 + 4i that is 5∠53.13°.

mainEntity.name: How do you find the angle of a complex number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use atan2(b, a), which gives the correct quadrant. For −3 − 4i the angle is −126.87°, not 53.13°.

mainEntity.name: What is the square root of a complex number?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are two, opposite in sign. √(3 + 4i) = ±(2 + i), because (2 + i)² = 3 + 4i. The nth roots come from De Moivre's theorem.

mainEntity.name: How do you find the nth roots of a complex number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take the nth root of the modulus and use angles (θ + 360°k) ÷ n for k = 0 to n − 1. The cube roots of 1 are at 0°, 120° and 240°.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between i and j?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing mathematically. Engineers use j so that i can mean current. Both satisfy j² = i² = −1.

mainEntity.name: How do you work out powers of i?

acceptedAnswer.text: They repeat every four: i, −1, −i, 1. Divide the exponent by 4 and use the remainder, so i²⁷ = i³ = −i.
